message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"e7a0ca76f35c70531dcabb0de86d6436cbc027deb4b3c822c2ad742d702d6f94","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-al-class-d:lineage:59","source_registry_sha256":"ea8231e949706ecda9f2a398d6eaf9ab30e224ac7defb0e6291b764b84ed0d95","units":[{"unit_id":"sec02-u01","module_id":"sec02-m01","objective_ids":["sec02-u01"],"title":{"text":"Test day, step by step","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Knowing the order of the vision, knowledge and road tests helps you arrive ready, with the right lenses, papers and vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-R06","sec02-F08","sec02-F10"]},{"text":"Lens rules decide whether you can even finish the test, so they matter before any driving starts.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Jordan is sixteen, already restricted to glasses, and brings a rented car to the road test with her mother.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F08","sec02-F10"]},"reasoning":{"text":"She must wear her glasses during the test, her mother must come along, and the rental counts only if Jordan is named on the agreement as an additional driver.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F08","sec02-F10"]},"result":{"text":"If Jordan is on the rental agreement and shows insurance and registration, she can take the road test as planned.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F09"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a lens requirement only matters during the road test.","fact_ids":["sec02-R07","sec02-F02"]},"correction":{"text":"When the vision exam shows you need lenses, you must wear them every time you drive, not only on test day.","fact_ids":["sec02-F02","sec02-R07"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Lenses on, papers ready, examiner last.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F10","sec02-F08"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"An applicant passes the knowledge test and pays the fee. Which license does that step earn?","fact_ids":["sec02-F05","sec02-R06"]},"answer":{"text":"The learner license.","fact_ids":["sec02-F05","sec02-R06"]},"rationale":{"text":"The knowledge test and fee lead to the learner license; the regular license waits for the road test.","fact_ids":["sec02-F05","sec02-R06"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Your test day in order","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F08","sec02-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Vision first, then knowledge, then road.","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F08","sec02-F02"]},{"text":"Bring lenses, papers and a safe car.","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F08","sec02-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson walks you through the steps of getting licensed in Alabama, in the order you will meet them. First comes a vision screening, which decides whether you need corrective lenses. Next is the knowledge test, which asks about Alabama traffic laws, road signs and safe-driving rules taken from this manual. Last comes the road test, given by a driver license examiner, which is the final step before driving on public roads. Along the way you will need the right lenses, the right papers and a vehicle that passes a quick safety check. Let us take each step in turn.","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F08","sec02-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Two different lens rules","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-R07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Restricted to lenses: wear them on the road test.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-R07"]},{"text":"Exam finds you need lenses: wear them always.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-R07"]}],"narration":{"text":"There are two lens rules, and they are easy to blur together. If your license is already restricted to corrective lenses, you must wear them during the road test. Separately, if the vision exam shows that lenses help you see better, you will be required to wear them whenever you drive, on every trip and not just on test day. And if you fail the vision exam, you see a licensed eye specialist and bring the report back to the examiner. If that report shows you see well enough to drive safely, you may go on and finish the test.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-R07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"What the knowledge test covers","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Alabama laws, road signs, safe-driving rules.","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07"]},{"text":"Questions come from this manual.","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"The knowledge test is built from this manual. It asks about Alabama traffic laws, road signs and safe-driving rules, so studying these chapters is the way to prepare. Automated testing is offered to every applicant who takes the knowledge test. If you are applying for a learner license, you receive it after passing the knowledge test and paying the fee. Someone who wants both a motor driven cycle license and a learner license must take both exams, and anyone applying for a cycle or motorcycle license studies the separate motorcycle manual as well.","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The road test and your car","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10","sec02-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"The examiner checks brake lights, signals, horn.","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10","sec02-F05"]},{"text":"Show insurance and registration.","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10","sec02-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"The road test is given by a driver license examiner and is the last step toward driving on public roads. If you are sixteen, a parent or guardian must come with you. Before you start, the examiner checks that the vehicle is safe and has working brake lights, left and right turn signals, and a horn. You must also show proof of insurance and registration for the car. A rental car is allowed only when you are named on the rental agreement as an additional driver. A regular-license applicant receives the license after passing the road test and paying the fee.","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10","sec02-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Learner license versus regular","fact_ids":["sec02-R06","sec02-F05","sec02-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Knowledge test leads to the learner license.","fact_ids":["sec02-R06","sec02-F05","sec02-F08"]},{"text":"Road test leads to the regular license.","fact_ids":["sec02-R06","sec02-F05","sec02-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"A common slip on test questions is mixing up which test earns which license. Passing the knowledge test, with the fee, earns the learner license. The road test is the final step, and passing it with the fee earns the regular license. So if a question describes someone who has only passed the knowledge test, that person holds a learner license, not a regular one. Keep the order straight: vision screening, then the knowledge test that leads to the learner license, and finally the road test that leads to the regular license.","fact_ids":["sec02-R06","sec02-F05","sec02-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check your test-day order","fact_ids":["sec02-F05","sec02-R06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Which license follows the knowledge test?","fact_ids":["sec02-F05","sec02-R06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: an applicant passes the knowledge test and pays the fee. Which license does that step earn? Think it through before you hear the answer. The answer is the learner license. The knowledge test and the fee lead to the learner license, while the regular license comes only after the road test, which is the final step given by a driver license examiner. If you said regular license, go back and review the order of the tests, because that order is the backbone of this whole lesson and of many test questions.","fact_ids":["sec02-F05","sec02-R06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Ready for test day","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F04","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Right lenses, right papers, safe car.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F04","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10"]},{"text":"Knowledge first, road test last.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F04","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"To wrap up, test day follows a clear path. Vision comes first, and if you are restricted to lenses you wear them on the road test, while a vision exam finding means lenses for all driving. The knowledge test covers laws, signs and safe-driving rules from this manual and leads to the learner license. The road test comes last, given by an examiner, with a safety check of brake lights, signals and horn, and with your insurance and registration in hand. A sixteen-year-old brings a parent or guardian, and a rental counts only if you are named on it.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F04","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec02-u02","module_id":"sec02-m02","objective_ids":["sec02-u02"],"title":{"text":"Tires, seating and ID cards","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F11","sec02-F13"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Simple monthly tire checks and a correct seating position keep the car safe and the restraint system working.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Sam checks his tires on a cold morning and pushes a penny head first into the deepest groove.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12"]},"reasoning":{"text":"He matches the gauge reading to the number on the door-jamb sticker, and watches whether Lincoln's whole head shows.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12"]},"result":{"text":"Lincoln's whole head shows, so the tires are too worn and Sam must replace them before driving.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking the best time to check tire pressure is right after a long drive.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11"]},"correction":{"text":"The manual says to check pressure monthly with a gauge while the tires are cold.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Cold tires, penny test, sit tall.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"You push a penny into the deepest groove and see all of Lincoln's head. What does that tell you?","fact_ids":["sec02-F12"]},"answer":{"text":"The tires are too worn to drive on and need replacing.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12"]},"rationale":{"text":"A fully visible head means the tread is too shallow, so the tires must be replaced.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Car, seat and ID","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F15","sec02-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Two tire checks.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F15","sec02-F16"]},{"text":"How to sit, and who gets an ID card.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F15","sec02-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers a few practical rules from the testing chapter. First, two simple tire checks you can do yourself, one for air pressure and one for tread depth. Then, how to sit in the driver's seat so that the restraint system works and the controls are within easy reach. Finally, two rules that are not about driving technique at all: what happens when a driver seems to have an impairment that affects driving, and who uses a non-driver identification card instead of a license. Each rule is short, so focus on the exact details.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F15","sec02-F16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Two monthly tire checks","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12"]},"lines":[{"text":"Gauge the pressure while tires are cold.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12"]},{"text":"Penny test: Lincoln's head goes in first.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12"]}],"narration":{"text":"Check tire pressure every month with a gauge while the tires are cold, and match the reading to the pressure number printed on the sticker in the door jamb, adding or releasing air as needed. For tread depth, use the penny test. Insert a penny into the deepest groove with Lincoln's head going in first. If you can see his whole head, the tread is too worn and the tires need to be replaced before you drive on them. Pressure is about the air inside, tread is about the rubber outside, and both checks take only a minute.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Sitting for control","fact_ids":["sec02-F13","sec02-F14"]},"lines":[{"text":"Back against the seat, feet on the floor.","fact_ids":["sec02-F13","sec02-F14"]},{"text":"Heel down; wheel top below your chin.","fact_ids":["sec02-F13","sec02-F14"]}],"narration":{"text":"How you sit affects your safety. Sit upright with your back against the seat and your feet on the floor, because slouching can make the restraint system less effective in a crash. Keep your heel on the floor and let your foot pivot between the brake and the accelerator rather than lifting the whole leg. Set the steering wheel so its top is no higher than your shoulders and sits below your chin. These small adjustments keep you in control of the pedals and the wheel and let the seat belt and other restraints do their job.","fact_ids":["sec02-F13","sec02-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Medical review and ID cards","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Impairment may bring medical statements.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F16"]},{"text":"ID cards serve people who are not driving.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"Two rules here are often confused. A driver who seems to have an impairment that affects driving may need a physician's statement and periodic checks by an examiner, and failing to report the condition can lead to revocation of the license. That is about keeping a license. The non-driver identification card is something else. It needs the same identity proof as a license and serves people who cannot physically qualify, people with no current Alabama license, and people who are giving up driving. One rule protects the road, the other gives non-drivers an ID.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the penny test","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"What does Lincoln's whole head mean?","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: you push a penny into the deepest groove of your tire, head first, and you can see all of Lincoln's head. What does that tell you? Decide before the answer comes. The answer is that the tires are too worn to drive on and need replacing. When the whole head shows, the tread is too shallow to grip safely. Remember that this test is about tread depth. Air pressure is a separate check, done monthly with a gauge while the tires are cold, using the number on the door-jamb sticker. Both checks matter.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Small checks, big safety","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F15","sec02-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Cold-tire gauge, penny tread test.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F15","sec02-F16"]},{"text":"Sit tall; know who needs an ID card.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F15","sec02-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"To sum up: check tire pressure monthly with a gauge while the tires are cold, and use the penny test to see whether the tread is worn out. Sit upright with your back against the seat so restraints stay effective, keep your heel on the floor as your foot pivots, and keep the top of the wheel below your chin. A driver with an impairment that affects driving may need a physician's statement and examiner checks, and must report the condition. And remember that a non-driver ID card needs the same identity proof as a license.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F15","sec02-F16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec02-u03","module_id":"sec02-m03","objective_ids":["sec02-u03"],"title":{"text":"Renewal, grace and duplicates","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-F19"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Renewal deadlines decide whether your license is still valid, and mixing them up can leave you driving illegally.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F19","sec02-F21"]},{"text":"Knowing when to get a duplicate instead of a renewal saves a wasted trip.","fact_ids":["sec02-F22","sec02-R04"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Lee's license expired forty days ago and he has not renewed yet.","fact_ids":["sec02-F19","sec02-R01"]},"reasoning":{"text":"The sixty-day grace period after expiration is still running, and the license stays valid during it.","fact_ids":["sec02-F19","sec02-R01"]},"result":{"text":"Lee can renew now and his license is still valid, but once the grace period ends he must not drive until he renews.","fact_ids":["sec02-F19","sec02-F21"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking the three-year late-renewal window lets you keep driving on an expired license.","fact_ids":["sec02-R02","sec02-F21"]},"correction":{"text":"Renewal without an exam stays possible for three years, but you may not legally drive on an expired license.","fact_ids":["sec02-F20","sec02-F21","sec02-R02"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Before, grace, late: renew early, drive only while valid.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-R02"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A license expired two years ago. Can its holder renew without an exam, and from what date does the new license run?","fact_ids":["sec02-F20","sec02-R03"]},"answer":{"text":"Yes; the new license runs four years from the last expiration date.","fact_ids":["sec02-F20","sec02-R03"]},"rationale":{"text":"Renewal without an exam is allowed within three years after expiring, and a late renewal counts from the old expiration date.","fact_ids":["sec02-F20","sec02-R03"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Keeping your license current","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-F22"]},"lines":[{"text":"Four-year license, renewal windows.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-F22"]},{"text":"Duplicates for lost cards.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-F22"]}],"narration":{"text":"An Alabama license does not last forever, and this lesson is about keeping it current. You will learn how long a license is valid, how early you may renew, what grace period applies after it expires, and how long you can wait before an exam is needed again. You will also see who may renew by mail, and the difference between renewing a license and replacing a lost one with a duplicate. Several of these rules use days and years that are easy to mix up, so we will line them up carefully and point out the most common trap along the way.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-F22"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Four years and early renewal","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"A license lasts four years from issue.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-R03"]},{"text":"Renew within one hundred eighty days before.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"An Alabama license expires four years after it is issued. You may renew it any time within one hundred eighty days before the expiration date printed on it, so you do not have to wait until the last minute. Some people may renew by mail: military members and their dependents, college students, and others temporarily out of state for work, as long as their license with photo and signature was issued within the last four years. A normal renewal simply runs four years from issue, which is the baseline the later rules are measured against.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Grace period and late renewal","fact_ids":["sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-R01","sec02-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Sixty days after expiration: still valid.","fact_ids":["sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-R01","sec02-R03"]},{"text":"Up to three years: renew without an exam.","fact_ids":["sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-R01","sec02-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"After your license expires, state law gives a sixty-day grace period for renewal, and the license stays valid during that period. Beyond that, a license can still be renewed without an exam for up to three years after it expires. When you renew late, the new license runs four years from the last expiration date, not from the day you renew and not from the original issue date. So the one hundred eighty days come before expiration, the sixty days come right after it, and the three years are the outer limit for renewing without an exam.","fact_ids":["sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-R01","sec02-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Renewable is not drivable","fact_ids":["sec02-F21","sec02-R02","sec02-F19"]},"lines":[{"text":"Late renewal does not allow driving.","fact_ids":["sec02-F21","sec02-R02","sec02-F19"]},{"text":"Only the grace period keeps you valid.","fact_ids":["sec02-F21","sec02-R02","sec02-F19"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Because renewal is possible for up to three years after expiration, some drivers assume they may keep driving during that time. They may not. You may not legally drive on an expired license, even though you can still renew it without an exam. Only the sixty-day grace period keeps the license valid after expiration. Once that grace period has passed, the license is expired for driving purposes until you renew it. Keep the two ideas apart: one window is about renewing, and only the short grace period is about driving.","fact_ids":["sec02-F21","sec02-R02","sec02-F19"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Duplicates and false affidavits","fact_ids":["sec02-F22","sec02-F23","sec02-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Lost or damaged, unexpired: get a duplicate.","fact_ids":["sec02-F22","sec02-F23","sec02-R04"]},{"text":"Lying on an affidavit can mean charges.","fact_ids":["sec02-F22","sec02-F23","sec02-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"If your license is still unexpired but is lost, destroyed or unreadable, you replace it with a duplicate from the Probate Judge or License Commissioner. No exam is needed, but you must prove your identity, for example with a certified birth certificate. A duplicate is different from a renewal: the duplicate replaces an unexpired license that is lost or damaged, while a renewal replaces one that is expiring or expired. Be honest in the process. Using a false affidavit to get a duplicate can bring forgery or perjury charges, or both, punished by a fine, prison or both.","fact_ids":["sec02-F22","sec02-F23","sec02-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check a late renewal","fact_ids":["sec02-F20","sec02-R03","sec02-F21"]},"lines":[{"text":"Expired two years ago: exam needed?","fact_ids":["sec02-F20","sec02-R03","sec02-F21"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a license expired two years ago. Can its holder renew without an exam, and from what date does the new license run? Work it out first. The answer is yes, the holder can renew without an exam, because that is allowed within three years after the license expires. The new license runs four years from the last expiration date, not from the renewal day. Remember, though, that being able to renew is not the same as being allowed to drive. The holder may not drive on the expired license in the meantime.","fact_ids":["sec02-F20","sec02-R03","sec02-F21"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Your renewal timeline","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-F21","sec02-F22","sec02-F23"]},"lines":[{"text":"One hundred eighty days before; sixty after.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-F21","sec02-F22","sec02-F23"]},{"text":"Three years to renew; duplicates for lost cards.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-F21","sec02-F22","sec02-F23"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us line up the timeline one last time. A license lasts four years from issue, and you may renew within one hundred eighty days before it expires, or by mail if you qualify while temporarily out of state. After expiration a sixty-day grace period keeps the license valid. Renewal without an exam stays possible for three years, with the new term counted from the last expiration date, but driving on an expired license is never allowed.
